endpoints.summary: Physician creates a new visit (status IN_PROGRESS) for either an app-user patient (patientUserId) or a physician-owned local chart (clinicPatientId). Returns the created Visit row with three shallow relation objects. Sets visitDate to server now, bumps ClinicPatient.lastVisitDate when a clinicPatientId is given, and writes a fire-and-forget audit row.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer, req.user = decoded token. Then auditLog('CREATE','visit') wraps res.json. NO userType check at all: any authenticated user reaches the handler; the gate is (a) a PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id -> otherwise 400 'Physician profile required' (NOT 403), and (b) prisma.clinic.findFirst({id: clinicId, physicianId: physician.id}) -> otherwise 403 'Not your clinic'. There is NO check that the physician is connected to the patient, and NO ownership check on clinicPatientId.
requestBody: patientUserId: string — required unless clinicPatientId is supplied
clinicPatientId: string — required unless patientUserId is supplied
appointmentId: string (optional) — READ but NEVER PERSISTED; used only to look up Appointment.subprofileId
dbWrites: visits — INSERT (prisma.visit.create). NOT in a transaction.
clinic_patients — UPDATE lastVisitDate = now(), only when body.clinicPatientId is truthy; awaited but wrapped in .catch(() => {}) so failures are silent and do not affect the 201.

activity_logs — INSERT via auditLog middleware (action 'CREATE', resource 'visit', resourceId = response body id, metadata {method:'POST', path:req.originalUrl}, ipAddress, userAgent sliced to 256). Fire-and-forget, .catch(() => {}). Only written when res.statusCode < 400 AND req.user?.id is set.
crossModelReads: ClinicPatient (findUnique by clinicPatientId — only when clinicPatientId given and patientUserId absent)
sideEffects: No notifications, no cache invalidation, no external calls
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header is missing or does not start with 'Bearer '
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws (bad signature/expired/malformed)
400 {"error":"clinicId is required"} when body.clinicId is falsy (checked BEFORE the patient check)
400 {"error":"patientUserId or clinicPatientId is required"} when BOTH body.patientUserId and body.clinicPatientId are falsy
400 {"error":"Physician profile required"} when no PhysicianProfile row exists for req.user.id — note 400, not 403
403 {"error":"Not your clinic"} when no Clinic matches { id: clinicId, physicianId: physician.id } (covers both 'clinic does not exist' and 'clinic belongs to someone else' — same body for both)

500 {"error":"Failed to create visit"} on any thrown error (FK violation on clinicId/organizationId/subprofileId/clinicPatientId, invalid enum, Prisma validation). No detail/details key is added on this route.
quirks: GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER (server/src/index.js L55-L81) mutates req.body BEFORE this handler for every request. It recursively walks strings/arrays/objects and: strips <script>...</script> blocks; strips opening/closing tags for script|iframe|embed|object|applet|form|input|textarea|select|button|link|meta|base|style; REMOVES any /\bon\w+\s*=\s*("..."|'...'|[^\s>]*)/gi match — so clinical prose like 'onset = 3 days ago' becomes ' days ago'; removes /(?:javascript|data|vbscript)\s*:/gi — so 'data: 2 units' becomes ' 2 units'; removes 'expression('; and REPLACES /url\s*\(/gi with the literal 'url\\(' (inserts a backslash). The .NET port must reproduce this exactly or chiefComplaint/rawNotes will differ byte-for-byte. Query params and route params are NOT sanitized.

`appointmentId` is accepted in the body but the Visit model has NO appointmentId column. It is used ONLY to fetch Appointment.subprofileId for auto-propagation, then discarded. The link between visit and appointment is never persisted anywhere.

Auto-propagation of subprofileId: only runs when body.subprofileId is falsy AND body.appointmentId is truthy. The appointment lookup is wrapped in a bare try/catch that swallows everything (`catch { }`), and there is no ownership check on the appointment — any appointmentId from any tenant can donate its subprofileId.

clinicPatientId fallback is a data-integrity landmine: when clinicPatientId is given without patientUserId, `resolvedPatientUserId = cp?.linkedUserId || userId`. If the ClinicPatient does not exist, or exists but has no linkedUserId, the visit's patientUserId is silently set to THE PHYSICIAN'S OWN userId. No 404, no error. Consequence: the physician then satisfies the `visit.patientUserId === userId` gate on PATCH /:id/patient-note, PUT /:id/patient-feedback and DELETE /:id/patient-dismiss for that visit, and VISIT_COMPLETED notifications for it are sent to the physician.
No ownership/tenancy check on clinicPatientId — a physician can attach another physician's ClinicPatient to their visit (and bump its lastVisitDate).

patientUserId has NO foreign key and NO relation in the Prisma schema (just `patientUserId String` + @@index). Any arbitrary string is accepted and stored; there is no validation that the user exists or is connected to the physician, despite the docstring claiming 'must be connected to the patient'.

Empty-string coalescing: chiefComplaint, rawNotes, subprofileId and clinicPatientId all go through `x || null`, so '' is stored as NULL, not ''. AppointmentsPage.jsx sends `chiefComplaint: appt.reason || ''`, which therefore lands as null.
visitDate is always `new Date()` on the server. A client-supplied visitDate is ignored (not even read).
organizationId is derived from the clinic row, never from the JWT.
status is not settable — always the schema default IN_PROGRESS.

The response's `clinic` object has only { name } and `subprofile` only { name, relation }. This is narrower than every other visit endpoint in the file. A .NET port that reuses one shared VisitDto here will emit extra keys (clinic.id, subprofile.id) and break byte-identity.
No transaction: visit INSERT and the clinic_patients UPDATE are two separate statements, and the second silently swallows failures.
auditLog's res.json override reads `req.params?.id || data?.id`; for POST there is no params.id so the audit resourceId is the newly created visit id.
auditLog also appends `reason` to metadata when req.body.reason exists — visits never send it, but a client that did would get it logged.

The response is the raw Prisma object serialized by Express's JSON.stringify: Prisma truncates Postgres timestamps to millisecond precision, so .NET must emit exactly 3 fractional digits + 'Z' (never 7 digits, never an offset like +00:00).

endpoints.summary: Owning physician updates visit documentation. Two distinct branches: (A) if visit.status === 'COMPLETED', ONLY followUpDate/followUpNotes may be edited (anything else -> 400), and a FOLLOW_UP_SET notification fires when the date actually changes; (B) otherwise a field-by-field patch of raw notes, SOAP, metadata, follow-up and specialtyData. Both branches respond with the full raw Visit row (no relations, no message key).
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401 on failure). No auditLog. In-handler: visit must exist (404 first), then a PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND visit.physicianId must equal physician.id, else 403 'Not your visit'. Patients can never reach a 2xx here. NOTE the check order is visit-then-physician, the OPPOSITE of DELETE /:id.
requestBody: diagnosis: string[] (optional) — Postgres String[]; a non-array value causes a Prisma error -> 500
diagnosisCodes: Json (optional) — usually [{code, description}]; client sends [] when empty
followUpDate: string|null (optional) — client sends 'YYYY-MM-DD' or null
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE (single statement, NOT in a transaction). Branch A writes only followUpDate/followUpNotes; branch B writes only the keys present in the body.
notifications — INSERT (branch A only, when the follow-up date actually changed), via notificationService.createNotification; whole block wrapped in try/catch so failures never affect the 200.
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId, for the ownership gate)
PhysicianProfile again inside the branch-A notification block, this time with include:{user:{select:{displayName}}} — a shadowing re-fetch of the same row
User (inside createNotification, to resolve email/displayName when sendEmail)
sideEffects: Branch A only: FOLLOW_UP_SET notification row + email to visit.patientUserId + push attempt. Title 'Follow-up Date Set'. Message: `Dr. ${physician?.user?.displayName || 'Your doctor'} has scheduled a follow-up for ${fDate}.` plus ` Note: ${followUpNotes}` appended when followUpNotes is truthy. data = { visitId, followUpDate } where followUpDate is the RAW CLIENT STRING, not the normalized Date.
Branch B: no notifications, no side effects at all.
No cache invalidation anywhere (GET /follow-ups-due is cached 30s and is NOT invalidated by this write).
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when prisma.visit.findUnique({where:{id}}) returns null — note NO deletedAt filter, so soft-deleted (deletedAt set) and ARCHIVED visits ARE found and ARE editable
403 {"error":"Not your visit"} when the caller has no PhysicianProfile OR visit.physicianId !== physician.id (same body for both — a patient calling this always gets 403, never 200)
400 {"error":"Cannot edit a completed visit"} when visit.status === 'COMPLETED' and the body is not follow-up-only (see quirks for the exact predicate)
500 {"error":"Failed to update visit"} on any thrown error — including a bad `diagnosis` type, an unparseable followUpDate producing Invalid Date, or a Prisma validation error
quirks: GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER applies here too (see POST / quirk 1). It runs over rawNotes, rawTranscript, chiefComplaint, all four SOAP fields, followUpNotes, and every string inside diagnosis[] / diagnosisCodes / specialtyData. The 'on\w+=' rule is the dangerous one for clinical text ('onset = ...' loses the value); the 'url(' -> 'url\\(' rule silently inserts a backslash.

`!== undefined` semantics: JSON has no undefined, so the effective rule is 'key PRESENT in the JSON body'. `null` counts as present. The port must distinguish absent-key from null-value per field, not use a nullable-DTO-with-defaults.

THE isFollowUpOnly PREDICATE OMITS specialtyData. It is: (followUpDate !== undefined || followUpNotes !== undefined) && rawNotes/rawTranscript/chiefComplaint/diagnosis/diagnosisCodes/subjective/objective/assessment/plan ALL === undefined. specialtyData is NOT in that exclusion list. So PUT on a COMPLETED visit with body {followUpNotes:'x', specialtyData:{...}} returns 200 and SILENTLY DROPS specialtyData (branch A builds followUpData from only the two follow-up fields). The same body without followUpDate/followUpNotes returns 400.
Branch A applies ONLY followUpDate/followUpNotes even though other recognized keys may have been present-but-ignored — no error, no warning.
The 'completed' guard checks ONLY status === 'COMPLETED'. ARCHIVED and CANCELLED visits fall through to branch B and are fully editable, including their SOAP notes.

followUpDate parsing: `new Date(followUpDate)`. The client sends a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD', which JS parses as UTC midnight -> stored 'YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z'. .NET's DateTime.Parse on a date-only string yields LOCAL midnight — the port MUST force UTC or every follow-up date shifts by the server offset.
followUpDate falsy coalescing: `followUpDate ? new Date(followUpDate) : null` — so '' and null both clear the column. But `0` and `false` would also clear it.

Notification-change detection compares apples to oranges: oldDate = visit.followUpDate.toISOString().split('T')[0] (a 'YYYY-MM-DD' UTC date string) vs newDate = the raw client string. If a client ever sends a full ISO datetime, newDate !== oldDate is always true and the FOLLOW_UP_SET notification+email re-fires on every autosave. The client autosaves every 3 seconds while editing.
Clearing the follow-up date (followUpDate: null) sends NO notification, because the guard is `if (newDate && newDate !== oldDate)`.

The notification's human date uses `new Date(followUpDate).toLocaleDateString('en-US', {weekday:'long',month:'long',day:'numeric',year:'numeric'})` — evaluated in the SERVER's timezone, so a UTC-midnight date renders as the previous day on any negative-offset server. Format example: 'Thursday, September 10, 2026'.
Inside the branch-A notification block a new `const physician` SHADOWS the outer one and re-queries PhysicianProfile with the user include — an extra DB round trip on every follow-up-date change.
An empty JSON body ({}) on a non-completed visit yields updateData = {} and still issues prisma.visit.update, which bumps updatedAt (@updatedAt) and returns 200 with a new updatedAt.
`diagnosis` (String[]) and `diagnosisCodes` (Json?) are different types with confusingly similar names; the client only ever sends diagnosisCodes.

Passing diagnosisCodes: null hits Prisma's nullable-Json path (NullableJsonNullValueInput) — the port must write SQL NULL, and the response must serialize `diagnosisCodes: null` (not the JSON literal string "null").
Response leaks rawNotes/rawTranscript/audioUrl — acceptable only because the gate is physician-only; the port must not add its own patient-safe stripping here.
No transaction and no optimistic concurrency: the 3-second client autosave plus a manual save can interleave and last-write-wins per whole-row update.

endpoints.summary: Owning physician marks the visit COMPLETED, stamps completedAt, and stores the M1.7 sharedSections whitelist controlling which SOAP sections the patient may see. Then fires a cascade of independently-try/caught side effects: patient VISIT_COMPLETED notification+email, per-staff VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF notifications, waiting-room auto-completion, and two blocks that are DEAD CODE. Responds with the full Visit row plus a trailing `message` key.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401). No auditLog. In-handler: visit must exist (404), then PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND visit.physicianId === physician.id, else 403 'Not your visit'. Visit-then-physician order.
endpoints.responseShape:
// The full raw Visit row (post-update) spread, with `message` appended LAST.
{
  "id": "<uuid>",
  "organizationId": "<uuid>",
  "clinicId": "<uuid>",
  "physicianId": "<uuid>",
  "patientUserId": "<string>",
  "subprofileId": "<uuid>|null",
  "clinicPatientId": "<uuid>|null",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
  "audioUrl": "<string>|null",
  "rawTranscript": "<string>|null",
  "rawNotes": "<string>|null",
  "subjective": "<string>|null",
  "objective": "<string>|null",
  "assessment": "<string>|null",
  "plan": "<string>|null",
  "chiefComplaint": "<string>|null",
  "diagnosis": ["<string>"],
  "diagnosisCodes": null,
  "followUpDate": "<iso>|null",
  "followUpNotes": "<string>|null",
  "sharedSections": null,
  "patientFeedback": "<string>|null",
  "patientFeedbackAt": "<iso>|null",
  "patientDismissedAt": "<iso>|null",
  "visitDate": "<iso>",
  "specialtyData": null,
  "completedAt": "2026-09-03T10:11:12.345Z",
  "createdAt": "<iso>",
  "updatedAt": "<iso>",
  "deletedAt": "<iso>|null",
  "message": "Visit completed and shared with patient"
}

// `sharedSections` is EITHER null (share all sections) OR the filtered client array,
//    e.g. ["subjective","assessment","plan"]. It is NEVER [] — an empty result is coerced to null.
//    Order and duplicates from the client array are preserved verbatim after filtering.
// `status` is always "COMPLETED" and `completedAt` always the server 'now' of this request.
// `message` is the LAST key (object spread then literal), which matters for byte-identical output.
// No relations are included.
requestBody: sharedSections: string[]|null|absent (optional) — subset of ['subjective','objective','assessment','plan']; anything not an array is treated as 'share all'
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE { status:'COMPLETED', completedAt: now(), sharedSections: <array|null> }. NOT in a transaction.
appointments — UPDATE { status:'COMPLETED' } — DEAD CODE, never executes (see quirks).
notifications — INSERT one VISIT_COMPLETED for the patient (try/caught).
notifications — INSERT one VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF per active ClinicStaff row, sequentially in a for-await loop (try/caught as a whole block).
waiting_queues — updateMany { status:'COMPLETED', completedAt: now() } for matching rows (try/caught).
payments — updateMany { visitId: id } — DEAD CODE, never executes (see quirks).
device_tokens — deleteMany possible inside pushService when a token is rejected.
crossModelReads: ClinicStaff (findMany where { clinicId: visit.clinicId, isActive: true }, select userId)
User (findUnique by visit.patientUserId, select displayName — for the staff message; and again inside createNotification for email)
externalDeps: notificationService.createNotification (required twice: once for patient, once per staff member)
sideEffects:
Patient notification: type 'VISIT_COMPLETED', title 'Visit Summary Available', message 'Your visit summary is now available. Check your health records for details.', data { visitId }, sendEmail true (subject = title, html '

{title}

{message}

').

Staff notifications: type 'VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF', title 'Visit Completed', message `${patientUser?.displayName || 'Patient'}'s visit is done${followUpText}` where followUpText = ` — Follow-up: ${new Date(updated.followUpDate).toLocaleDateString()}` (EM DASH U+2014, server locale/TZ) when updated.followUpDate is truthy, else ''. data { visitId, patientUserId, followUpDate: updated.followUpDate (a Date, serialized into the notification JSON), clinicId }. sendEmail defaults false but push is still attempted.

Waiting-room auto-complete: waitingQueue rows for { clinicId: visit.clinicId, patientUserId: visit.patientUserId, queueDate between local-midnight and local-23:59:59.999, status in ['WAITING','BEING_SEEN'] } get status 'COMPLETED' and completedAt now().
Every side-effect block is individually try/caught and logged — NONE of them can turn the 200 into an error.
No cache invalidation (GET /follow-ups-due is cached 30s and is not busted).
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when findUnique returns null — NO deletedAt filter, so soft-deleted and ARCHIVED visits are found and CAN be completed
403 {"error":"Not your visit"} when the caller has no PhysicianProfile OR visit.physicianId !== physician.id
500 {"error":"Failed to complete visit"} only if the main prisma.visit.update itself throws — every downstream side effect is swallowed
quirks: DEAD CODE #1: `if (visit.appointmentId)` — the Visit model has NO appointmentId column, so visit.appointmentId is ALWAYS undefined. The 'auto-complete the linked appointment' block NEVER runs. Appointments are never auto-completed by completing a visit, despite the comment.

DEAD CODE #2: the same undefined visit.appointmentId guards the 'Link existing payment to this visit' block, so payments are NEVER linked to a visit here. A faithful port must reproduce the no-op; 'fixing' it changes observable data.

EMPTY ARRAY MEANS SHARE EVERYTHING. `sectionsToStore = sharedSections.filter(valid); if (length === 0) sectionsToStore = null;` and null means 'all sections visible to the patient' in GET /:id. The React client builds the array from checkbox state (`Object.entries(shareSelections).filter(([,v]) => v).map(([k]) => k)`), so a physician who UNCHECKS EVERY SECTION shares ALL sections. This is a real privacy inversion the port must copy.
Any non-array sharedSections (missing key, null, a string, an object) leaves sectionsToStore = null -> share all. Only Array.isArray is checked.

Invalid entries are silently dropped; DUPLICATES AND CLIENT ORDER ARE PRESERVED — ['plan','plan','subjective'] is stored and echoed back verbatim as ["plan","plan","subjective"]. Do not dedupe or sort in the port.
The valid set is ['subjective','objective','assessment','plan'] — lowercase, exact match via Array.includes (case-sensitive). 'Subjective' is dropped.

Writing `sharedSections: null` targets a nullable Json column (Prisma NullableJsonNullValueInput). The port must persist SQL NULL (not the JSON literal null) and serialize it back as `"sharedSections": null`.

NO IDEMPOTENCY GUARD: there is no check on the current status. Re-completing an already COMPLETED (or ARCHIVED, or CANCELLED) visit succeeds, RESETS completedAt to now, OVERWRITES sharedSections, and RE-FIRES the patient email plus all staff notifications and the waiting-room update. The client calls handleSave() then /complete, so a double-click sends two rounds.

The waiting-room day window is built with `new Date(y, m, d)` and `new Date(y, m, d, 23,59,59,999)` — SERVER LOCAL midnight — but queueDate is stored as UTC. On a non-UTC server the window is offset and can miss or over-match rows. Reproduce with server-local boundaries, not UTC ones.

The staff notification message uses `.toLocaleDateString()` with NO locale and NO options — output depends entirely on the server's ICU locale/TZ (typically 'M/D/YYYY' on en-US). The separator before it is ' — ' with an EM DASH (U+2014), not a hyphen.
Staff notifications are created SEQUENTIALLY with await in a for-loop; a clinic with many staff members serializes that many notification inserts (plus a push attempt each) inside the request.
The patient notification goes to visit.patientUserId, which for an unlinked local ClinicPatient visit is THE PHYSICIAN'S OWN userId (see POST / quirk) — the physician emails themselves.
createNotification always attempts pushService.send even when sendEmail is false; failures are swallowed unless the message mentions 'findMany'.
The response spread puts `message` after `deletedAt`. Prisma key order for the visit scalars is the schema declaration order listed in responseShape.

GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER also walks the sharedSections array elements (sanitizeValue maps arrays) before this handler sees them — harmless for the four valid keywords, but the port should know the array is sanitized, not raw.

endpoints.summary: Physician 'deletes' a visit — but it is a status-only archive: sets status = 'ARCHIVED' and nothing else. deletedAt is NOT touched, no rows cascade, nothing is destroyed. Returns a plain message object.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401). No auditLog on this route (despite being the destructive one). In-handler: PhysicianProfile is looked up FIRST — no profile => 403 'Physician access required'. Only THEN is the visit fetched (404), then ownership (403 'Not your visit'). This physician-then-visit order is the REVERSE of PUT /:id and PUT /:id/complete and is observable.
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE { status: 'ARCHIVED' }. Single statement, NOT in a transaction. deletedAt is left untouched (stays null), and no child rows (prescriptions, investigations, payments, inventoryTransactions) are affected.
sideEffects: None. No notification to the patient, no audit row, no cache invalidation.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws

403 {"error":"Physician access required"} when no PhysicianProfile exists for req.user.id — RETURNED BEFORE the visit is even looked up, so a patient (or a bogus id) gets 403 here where every other route in the file would 404
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when the visit does not exist (only reachable by an actual physician)
403 {"error":"Not your visit"} when visit.physicianId !== physician.id
500 {"error":"Failed to archive visit"} on any thrown error
quirks: The JSDoc above the handler is a LIE: it says 'permanently deletes a visit and all related records (prescriptions, investigations cascade-delete via Prisma schema)'. The body does a status update only. Port the code, not the comment.

deletedAt is NOT set. Because softDeleteFilter is { deletedAt: null }, an ARCHIVED visit still passes the soft-delete filter everywhere. It disappears from the physician list only because GET / applies status: { not: 'ARCHIVED' } when no explicit status filter is given — and it REAPPEARS if the client passes ?status=ARCHIVED.

The patient KEEPS SEEING the visit: GET / for non-physicians filters status: { in: ['COMPLETED','ARCHIVED'] }, so archiving does not hide it from the patient. Only DELETE /:id/patient-dismiss does that.
Re-archiving an already-ARCHIVED visit succeeds with the same 200 body (bumping updatedAt). No idempotency guard, no 409.
No status precondition: an IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED visit can be archived directly, and PUT /:id will then still happily edit it (the edit guard only blocks status === 'COMPLETED').
Route order: this DELETE '/:id' is registered at L1342, before DELETE '/:id/patient-dismiss' at L1419, but Express matches on segment count so there is no shadowing between them.
No audit row is written even though POST / has auditLog — the destructive route is the unaudited one.
No body and no query params are read; a request body is ignored (but still sanitized by the global middleware).

endpoints.summary: Patient saves (or clears) their own free-text note on a visit. Reuses the SAME Visit.patientFeedback / patientFeedbackAt columns as PUT /:id/patient-feedback, but with different validation, different response shape, and NO physician notification. Returns a 3-key projection.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401). No auditLog. In-handler: visit must exist (404), then visit.patientUserId must equal req.user.id, else 403 'Not your visit'. NO userType check — anyone whose id happens to be the visit's patientUserId passes, including a physician on an unlinked-ClinicPatient visit (see POST / quirk). NO status check: an IN_PROGRESS visit can be annotated.
requestBody: note: string|null|absent — the note text. NOT trimmed. Falsy (absent, null, '') clears BOTH columns.
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE { patientFeedback: note || null, patientFeedbackAt: note ? now() : null }. Single statement, no transaction.
sideEffects: NONE. Unlike PUT /:id/patient-feedback, which writes the same two columns, this route sends NO PATIENT_FEEDBACK notification to the physician. A note saved here is invisible in the physician's notification feed.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when findUnique returns null — NO deletedAt filter and NO status filter
403 {"error":"Not your visit"} when visit.patientUserId !== req.user.id (the owning physician gets 403 here unless they are also the recorded patientUserId)
500 {"error":"Failed to save note"} on any thrown error — e.g. `note` sent as a number or object, which Prisma rejects for a String column
quirks: SILENT CLEAR ON EMPTY: `note || null` plus `note ? new Date() : null` means PATCH with { note: '' } (or {} or { note: null }) WIPES the patient's existing note and its timestamp, returning 200 with both keys null. There is no confirm, no distinct status.

NO TRIM: whitespace-only '   ' is truthy, so it is stored verbatim as '   ' and patientFeedbackAt is stamped. The sibling PUT /:id/patient-feedback rejects the same input with 400 — the two endpoints validate the same column differently.

COLUMN COLLISION: this route and PUT /:id/patient-feedback both own Visit.patientFeedback/patientFeedbackAt. Whichever fires last wins, and only the /patient-feedback path notifies the physician. Do not model these as two separate fields in the port.
NO STATUS GUARD: works on IN_PROGRESS, CANCELLED and ARCHIVED visits, while /patient-feedback requires status === 'COMPLETED'.
Response key name differs from the request key name: in `note`, out `patientFeedback`.
The response is a narrow `select` (id, patientFeedback, patientFeedbackAt) — NOT the full visit. Reusing a full VisitDto in the port breaks byte-identity here.
This is the only PATCH verb in the router; the client uses api.patch (VisitInboxPage.jsx L640). A .NET port must map the verb exactly — PUT will 404/405.

GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER runs on `note` before the handler: 'on\w+=' sequences are stripped, 'javascript:/data:/vbscript:' prefixes removed, and 'url(' becomes 'url\\('. Patient-authored prose is therefore not stored verbatim.
No audit row, no notification, no cache invalidation.
The comment claims 'These notes persist even if the physician archives the visit' — true only because DELETE /:id merely sets status = 'ARCHIVED' and patients still see ARCHIVED visits.

endpoints.summary: Patient attaches a post-visit note/question to a COMPLETED visit and the physician gets a PATIENT_FEEDBACK notification. Writes the same two columns as PATCH /:id/patient-note but trims, requires non-empty text and requires status COMPLETED. Returns a 2-key projection (no id).
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401). No auditLog. Validation order is unusual: the feedback-text check runs BEFORE the visit is fetched. Then visit must exist (404), then visit.patientUserId === req.user.id else 403 'Only the patient can leave feedback', then visit.status must be 'COMPLETED' else 400. No userType check.
requestBody: feedback: string — REQUIRED, must be non-empty after .trim(); stored TRIMMED
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE { patientFeedback: feedback.trim(), patientFeedbackAt: now() }. Single statement, no transaction.
notifications — INSERT one PATIENT_FEEDBACK row for the physician's userId (whole block try/caught, cannot fail the 200).
device_tokens — possible deleteMany inside pushService on a rejected token.
crossModelReads: User (findUnique by req.user.id, select displayName — for the notification message)
PhysicianProfile (findUnique by id: visit.physicianId, select userId — note: by PROFILE id, not userId)
sideEffects: Physician notification: userId = physicianProfile.userId, type 'PATIENT_FEEDBACK', title 'Patient Left Visit Feedback', message `${patient?.displayName || 'A patient'} left a note on a completed visit.`, data { visitId }, sendEmail FALSE — so no email, but a push is still attempted.
Skipped entirely (no notification) if the PhysicianProfile row cannot be found.
No email, no audit row, no cache invalidation.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
400 {"error":"Feedback text is required"} when body.feedback is falsy OR trims to '' — CHECKED FIRST, before the visit lookup, so a nonexistent visit id with an empty body returns 400, not 404
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when findUnique returns null — NO deletedAt filter
403 {"error":"Only the patient can leave feedback"} when visit.patientUserId !== req.user.id — note the wording differs from the 'Not your visit' used by every other route here
400 {"error":"Can only add feedback to completed visits"} when visit.status !== 'COMPLETED' (so ARCHIVED visits are rejected even though the patient can still see them in their inbox)

500 {"error":"Failed to save feedback"} on any thrown error — notably when `feedback` is a truthy non-string (e.g. a number), because `!feedback` is false and then `feedback.trim()` throws TypeError inside the try
quirks: VALIDATION ORDER IS OBSERVABLE: the 400 for empty feedback precedes the 404 for a missing visit and the 403 for wrong ownership. Empty text against someone else's visit returns 400, revealing nothing — but the port must not reorder these checks.

`feedback.trim()` is called twice conceptually — once for the guard, once for the stored value — so the STORED value is trimmed while PATCH /:id/patient-note stores untrimmed text into the SAME column.

TYPE HAZARD: a truthy non-string feedback (number 5, an object, an array) passes `!feedback` and then throws on .trim() -> 500 'Failed to save feedback'. Not a 400. The port must produce 500 for that input, not a model-binding 400.

COLUMN COLLISION with PATCH /:id/patient-note: both write Visit.patientFeedback and patientFeedbackAt. Only this route notifies the physician; the PATCH route can silently overwrite or clear what this one saved without any notification.
The response OMITS `id`, unlike the PATCH sibling. Two endpoints writing the same columns return two different shapes.
Response key differs from the request key: in `feedback`, out `patientFeedback`.
PhysicianProfile is looked up by `id: visit.physicianId` (the profile PK), not by userId — the port must not confuse the two id spaces.

The 'only the patient' gate is purely `visit.patientUserId === req.user.id`. For a visit created from an unlinked local ClinicPatient, POST / set patientUserId to the PHYSICIAN'S OWN userId, so the physician can leave 'patient feedback' on their own visit and then notify themselves.
Overwrites, not appends: each call replaces the whole note and re-stamps patientFeedbackAt, and re-fires the PATIENT_FEEDBACK notification. The client's Save Note button can be pressed repeatedly.
sendEmail is explicitly false here, but createNotification still always attempts pushService.send — so a push may go out with no email.

GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER mutates `feedback` before the handler: 'onset = ...' style text loses the value, 'javascript:/data:/vbscript:' are stripped, 'url(' becomes 'url\\(' — and this happens BEFORE the trim/empty check, so input consisting only of a stripped pattern (e.g. '<script>x</script>') can arrive as '' and yield 400 'Feedback text is required'.

Route registration: PUT '/:id' (L391) is registered before PUT '/:id/patient-feedback' (L611), but Express matches segment counts so there is no shadowing — '/:id' never captures 'x/patient-feedback'.

endpoints.summary: Patient hides a visit from their own inbox by stamping Visit.patientDismissedAt = now(). The row is untouched otherwise and stays fully visible to the physician. Returns a plain message object.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> JWT Bearer (401). No auditLog. In-handler: visit must exist (404), then visit.patientUserId must equal req.user.id, else 403 'Not your visit'. No userType check, no status check.
dbWrites: visits — UPDATE { patientDismissedAt: now() }. Single statement, no transaction. Result discarded.
sideEffects: None. No notification to the physician, no audit row, no cache invalidation.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header missing / not Bearer
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws
404 {"error":"Visit not found"} when findUnique returns null — NO deletedAt filter, NO status filter, and NO patientDismissedAt filter
403 {"error":"Not your visit"} when visit.patientUserId !== req.user.id
500 {"error":"Failed to remove visit"} on any thrown error
quirks: NOT IDEMPOTENT IN DATA: an already-dismissed visit can be dismissed again, and patientDismissedAt is OVERWRITTEN with the new now(). Same 200 body, different stored timestamp.

NO UNDISMISS ENDPOINT EXISTS anywhere in the router. Once stamped, the patient can never get the visit back into their inbox through the API (GET / hard-filters patientDismissedAt: null for non-physicians).

Asymmetric filtering: patientDismissedAt is applied ONLY in the non-physician branch of GET /. The physician list ignores it entirely, and GET /:id ignores it too — so a dismissed visit is still fetchable by direct id by the patient.

NO STATUS GUARD: a patient can dismiss an IN_PROGRESS visit they cannot even see in their list, pre-emptively hiding the summary before the physician completes it. Completing the visit later does NOT clear patientDismissedAt, so the VISIT_COMPLETED notification arrives for a visit that will never appear in the inbox.
The DELETE verb performs an UPDATE; nothing is deleted and deletedAt is not touched.
The update result is awaited and thrown away — the response never reflects the stored timestamp.

This route sits AFTER DELETE '/:id' (L1342) in registration order, but Express segment matching means '/:id' cannot shadow '/:id/patient-dismiss'. The path has exactly two segments after the mount point.
Mounted path seen by the client is DELETE /api/visits/:id/patient-dismiss (client/src/pages/VisitInboxPage.jsx L546); the client ignores the response body and only branches on success/failure.
No request body is read; any body sent is ignored (though still run through the global sanitizer).
